speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis (LAD) secondary to captopril therapy.

The sudden onset of painful blisters on the forearm, combined with mucosal involvement (oral and genital ulcers) shortly after starting captopril, strongly suggests a drug-induced autoimmune blistering disease. Given the negative history of poison ivy and the specific medication timeline, I suspect captopril is the culprit rather than an infection like HSV. Please confirm if you have noticed any new rash on your trunk or groin, and if you have seen any new medications added to your list besides the captopril and meloxicam changes.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please upload clear, close-up photos of the forearm blisters and the oral/genital ulcers to assess the "cluster of jewels" pattern often seen in LAD.
